title: Cure chronic hepatitis C across genotypes with finite oral therapy

concept.text: Eradicate chronic HCV infection using a finite, interferon-free oral regimen, with sustained virological response after treatment. Sofosbuvir enabled the transition; subsequent pan-genotypic combinations made cure routine across genotypes 1–6. Proposed completion test: FDA approval of an oral regimen covering HCV genotypes 1–6, supported by pivotal trials measuring undetectable or unquantifiable HCV RNA at least 12 weeks after treatment ends (SVR12). Test set by: FDA sets the approval decision; AASLD–IDSA defines SVR12 as 'consistent with cure of chronic HCV infection.' Reported achieved: FDA approved sofosbuvir (Sovaldi) on 6 December 2013; the pan-genotypic milestone was achieved by sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (Epclusa) approval on 28 June 2016. Sources given: [FDA Sovaldi approval documentation](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2013/204671Orig1s000AdminCorres.pdf) ; [FDA Epclusa approval package](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208341Orig1s000Approv.pdf) ; [AASLD–IDSA assessment of HCV cure](https://www.hcvguidelines.org/guidance/monitoring-patients-who-are-starting-hcv-treatment-are-on-treatment-or-have-completed-therapy/).

page.title: Pan-genotypic oral therapy for chronic hepatitis C
page.definition: A finite course of oral drugs without interferon cures chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection across genotypes 1–6, genetically distinct groups of the virus. Cure means undetectable or nonquantifiable HCV RNA at least 12 weeks after treatment ends, termed sustained virologic response (SVR12).

goal.need: Chronic HCV infection can cause cirrhosis and liver cancer. WHO reports that direct-acting antivirals cure more than 95% of people with HCV infection, but access to diagnosis and treatment remains limited.

figures.caption: Global HCV burden reported by WHO on 28 July 2026.
figures.note: These are population estimates, not counts from treatment trials.

statements.body: WHO recommends pan-genotypic antiviral treatment for chronic HCV infection.
statements.quote: WHO recommends therapy with pan-genotypic direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) for all adults, adolescents and children down to 3 years of age with chronic hepatitis C infection.

statements.body: The American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the Infectious Diseases Society of America identify virologic cure as the treatment goal.
statements.quote: The proximate goal of HCV therapy is SVR (virologic cure)

completion.title: FDA approves a finite interferon-free oral regimen for chronic HCV genotypes 1–6 on SVR12 evidence.
completion.criterion: FDA approval covers adults with chronic HCV genotype 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 infection, with a finite oral regimen supported by pivotal SVR12 results. The qualifying regimen is sofosbuvir/velpatasvir for 12 weeks without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis; its original indication also includes 12 weeks with oral ribavirin for decompensated cirrhosis. SVR12 means undetectable or nonquantifiable HCV RNA at least 12 weeks after treatment completion.
completion.set_by: FDA, NDA 208341 approval letter and original Epclusa prescribing information; AASLD–IDSA supplies the clinical definition of cure.
completion.threshold_quote: for the treatment of adult patients with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotypes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 infection:
completion.basis: Achieved on 28 June 2016 with FDA approval of Epclusa. The licence establishes the population, genotype coverage and finite regimen; AASLD–IDSA describes SVR12 as “consistent with cure of chronic HCV infection”.

milestones.title: An HCV antiviral produces 50% and 90% inhibition of viral RNA replication in cell culture.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate concentration-dependent antiviral activity in an HCV RNA replication model, establishing the concentrations producing 50% and 90% inhibition, EC50 and EC90. FDA specifies these measurements without a universal potency cutoff. A laboratory example published on 26 August 2010 is sofosbuvir, then PSI-7977: EC50 0.092 μM and EC90 0.29 μM in the clone A cell model containing replicating HCV RNA.
milestones.set_by: FDA, November 2017 HCV drug-development guidance, section II.A.1.b; this guidance states the laboratory development criterion after the cited demonstration.
milestones.threshold_quote: 50 and 90 percent effective concentrations (EC50 and EC90) should be determined.

milestones.title: Two days of an oral HCV protease inhibitor lower plasma HCV RNA in infected people.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate a reduction in plasma HCV RNA following two days of oral NS3 protease inhibition in people with chronic genotype 1 infection, the human proof-of-concept test used for BILN 2061. The 2004 clinical report describes three placebo-controlled studies with 31, 10 and 10 participants; most active-drug recipients had RNA reductions of 2–3 log10. Further development was suspended pending resolution of animal toxicity findings.
milestones.set_by: Boehringer Ingelheim and collaborating investigators, BILN 2061 proof-of-concept studies; the published test concerned genotype 1.
milestones.threshold_quote: established proof-of-concept in humans for an HCV NS3 protease inhibitor.

milestones.title: A finite interferon-free oral HCV regimen produces undetectable RNA 24 weeks after treatment.
milestones.criterion: Achieve the NIH phase 2a trial's SVR24 endpoint after 24 weeks of oral sofosbuvir plus ribavirin in previously untreated adults with chronic genotype 1 infection. The study enrolled 60 participants: 10 in an initial cohort and 25 in each randomized ribavirin-dose group. The report published on 28 August 2013 found SVR24 in 9/10, 17/25 and 12/25, respectively. These are observed response proportions, not a prespecified minimum cure rate.
milestones.set_by: NIH investigators, the phase 2a protocol's primary efficacy endpoint, published by Osinusi and colleagues; the test concerned genotype 1.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary study end point was the proportion of participants with undetectable HCV viral load 24 weeks after treatment completion

milestones.title: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir meets the pivotal ASTRAL SVR12 efficacy tests across HCV genotypes 1–6.
milestones.criterion: For adults without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis, 12-week sofosbuvir/velpatasvir achieves SVR12, HCV RNA <15 IU/mL. ASTRAL-1, covering genotypes 1, 2, 4–6, requires superiority to 85% by a two-sided exact binomial test at α=0.05. ASTRAL-2/3, covering genotypes 2/3, require the lower 95% confidence bound for the difference versus sofosbuvir/ribavirin to exceed −10 percentage points. FDA's 2016 review records success; responses were 618/624, 133/134 and 264/277, respectively.
milestones.set_by: FDA, accepted ASTRAL-1–3 protocol efficacy tests reproduced and evaluated in the NDA 208341 clinical review.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary hypothesis was that subjects in the SOF/VEL group would achieve an SVR12 rate superior to the performance goal of 85%,

results.finding: PSI-7977 inhibited HCV RNA replication in clone A cells, with an EC90 of 0.29 μM; assays used duplicate wells.
results.detail: The reported EC50 was 0.092 μM. The assay used serial drug dilutions and a no-drug control.

results.finding: In 51 patients with chronic genotype 1 HCV, most achieved viral RNA reductions of 2–3 log10 copies/mL.
results.detail: BILN 2061 was given for two days in three placebo-controlled studies. The report specifies serum viral RNA rather than plasma RNA and does not explicitly state the route of administration. Further trials were on hold pending resolution of animal toxicity issues.
results.quote: Viral RNA reductions of 2-3 log 10 copies/mL were achieved in most of the patients.

results.finding: ASTRAL-1: 618 of 624 adults receiving sofosbuvir/velpatasvir achieved SVR12.
results.detail: ASTRAL-1 met its superiority test, and ASTRAL-2 met its non-inferiority margin. The excerpt reports significant superiority in ASTRAL-3 but does not give its confidence bound. It defines SVR12 using the assay's lower limit of quantitation but does not state that this limit was 15 IU/mL.
